modules.title: 网页跨域请求为什么要先获得服务器允许
CORS 在请求链路中的位置

items.title: “源”由地址组成
items.text: 协议、域名或端口有一个不同，就可能是不同源。本地网页从 `localhost:3000` 调接口 `localhost:4000` 也是常见跨源场景。

items.title: 服务器声明允许范围
items.text: 浏览器读取响应前检查服务器的 CORS 响应头；服务端应只允许实际需要的站点、方法和凭据，而不是为了消除报错对所有来源开放。

modules.title: 容易混淆的地方
modules.text: CORS 不是认证、登录或数据库权限。即使浏览器被允许读取，服务端仍必须验证用户身份和操作权限；反过来，已登录用户也可能因为服务器没有允许当前网页来源而看到 CORS 报错。

lessonPractice.title: 本地网页 `localhost:3000` 调用 API `localhost:4000` 时，控制台报 CORS。哪项排查最准确？

options.label: 让 API 允许 `http://localhost:3000`，并核对当前请求的方法和凭据规则
options.feedback: 对。两个端口构成不同源，浏览器需要从 API 响应里看到对应的允许规则。

options.label: 把网页请求改成 `no-cors`，继续按原方式读取 API 返回的数据
options.feedback: `no-cors` 通常只会得到网页脚本无法读取的不透明响应，不能让原来的数据读取继续工作。

options.label: 让 API 允许 `http://localhost:4000`，因为请求最终发到了这个地址
options.feedback: CORS 要允许发起请求的网页来源，这里是 3000；4000 是被请求的 API 地址。

en.title: A local page at `localhost:3000` calls an API at `localhost:4000` and the console reports CORS. Which investigation is most accurate?

options.label: Allow `http://localhost:3000` at the API and verify the request method and credential rules
options.feedback: Correct. The two ports are different origins, and the browser needs matching permission in the API response.

options.label: Change the page request to `no-cors` and keep reading the API data in the same way
options.feedback: `no-cors` normally produces an opaque response that page script cannot read, so the original data flow still does not work.

options.label: Allow `http://localhost:4000` because that is the address receiving the request
options.feedback: CORS must allow the page origin that initiates the request, which is 3000 here; 4000 is the API destination.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 请排查本地页面 `http://localhost:3000` 请求接口 `http://localhost:4000` 的 CORS 报错。只允许当前开发页面需要的来源、方法和凭据，不要把所有来源都开放；改完后在浏览器实际发起一次请求验证。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: Investigate the CORS error when `http://localhost:3000` calls `http://localhost:4000`. Allow only the origin, methods, and credentials needed by this development page; do not open every origin. Then make a real browser request to verify it.

learning.assumes: You have seen a page call an API on another domain or a cross-origin error in the browser console.
learning.outcome: You can distinguish CORS from login, tokens, and backend authorization, then check which frontend origin and request type need permission.

modules.title: Why a cross-origin request needs server permission
Where CORS sits in the request path

items.title: An origin comes from the address
items.text: A different protocol, domain, or port can mean a different origin. A local page at `localhost:3000` calling `localhost:4000` is a common cross-origin case too.

items.title: The server declares the allowed scope
items.text: Before the browser exposes a response, it checks CORS response headers. A server should allow the real sites, methods, and credentials needed—not every origin just to remove an error.

modules.title: What it is not
modules.text: CORS is not authentication, login, or database authorization. Even when a browser may read a response, the server must verify identity and permission. Conversely, a signed-in user can still see a CORS error when the server did not allow the current page origin.

distinctions.label: Authentication
distinctions.text: {c:cors} decides whether browser code may read a cross-origin response. {c:authentication} identifies the requester, and passing both checks still does not grant business authorization.
